posts.title: A mini-textbook on consolidation accounting
posts.source_date_evidence: LinkedIn public SocialMediaPosting.datePublished metadata retrieved 26 October 2026
posts.original_post_text:
I was reminded yesterday that I wrote an online "mini-textbook" on consolidation accounting in 2024 and you can read it here: https://lnkd.in/eYT9xMv6

The source code is all here: https://lnkd.in/ekxxvXSJ
It is easy to render into a website or into a PDF.

My goal was to have material for teaching consolidations that wasn't embarrassingly awful and made it possible for a motivated student (i.e., a tiny, perhaps non-existent, minority) to get a comprehensible view on the topic.

(Note that one teaches consolidation accounting very differently in Australia under IFRS than one does in the US. Somehow US accounting textbooks seem to put a lot of the details outside both intermediate and advanced accounting.)

posts.title: Learning Python Polars
posts.source_date_evidence: LinkedIn public SocialMediaPosting.datePublished metadata retrieved 26 October 2026
posts.original_post_text:
Are you interested in learning Python Polars? Working with Martien Lubberink PhD, I have created a fast-paced introduction to the basics here: https://lnkd.in/eSNsmTe8

Why Python Polars? Because it's a very fast "next generation data frame library" [Wes McKinney] that can handle multi-gigabyte data files with ease.

One challenge with Python has traditionally been setting things up. Please provide feedback on the (draft!) instructions here: https://lnkd.in/ew3nJJaY

(Thanks to Konstantin Pavlenkov for providing detailed feedback on an earlier version of the materials linked to above.)

posts.title: `farr`: reusable code and teaching data
posts.source_date_evidence: LinkedIn public SocialMediaPosting.datePublished metadata retrieved 26 October 2026
posts.original_post_text:
I recently released an update of the R package "farr" that provides data and code to support the book "Empirical Research in Accounting: Tools and Methods" to CRAN: https://lnkd.in/d4mAVrRV

The update was needed in part to address changes in the upstream data sources (https://lnkd.in/dJGUQRww).

One benefit of putting data and code in an R package is that a function can be introduced in one chapter and used in another without having to repeat the code or introduce dependencies between chapters. Also, it's an easy way to distribute small-ish data sets to students.

Some of the functions and data might be of interest even for researchers not using the book, such as the winsorize() function and the GVKEY-CIK table, gvkey_ciks. (If using gvkey_ciks, install the GitHub version, as that table has been updated there and this update won't appear on CRAN till next month.)
